doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Count Basie offers him the lead trumpet chair
summary: His U.K. jazz band opened for Basie, who heard him play and invited him to lead trumpet; he declined.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: He asked me to play lead trumpet once. Count Basie.

In person. Because my jazz band was the warm-up act for Count Basie at U.K. So my students, you know I didn’t play with the band very often, ‘cause that would be a solo that they couldn’t play. I mean they wouldn’t be on stage learning. So — but after my first year there one of the students says, “Well you should play a solo with us.” You know they’d heard me play, I’d demonstrate, you know I’d say that phrase, let me play it it’ll take a lot less time to do this.

And they knew I could play. And after they heard me to play with Clark Terry because he asked me to play. That very first year that I played with him, that I was teaching. But the next year I wasn’t playing anything. They said, “How come you never play with us?” I said, “Well because you wouldn’t have a chance to play another solo, you know I like to feature one of you playing a solo, a saxophone, a trumpet, a trombone you know, and if we do that then there would be two trumpet solos and we don’t need that. We need — and I’ll feature different people as they’re able.” You know? So they said, “Yeah but you go all over the country and you play with other people’s bands, right?” And I was like oh my God that is so true. I never thought of it, you know what I mean? It was so simple. All I was worried about was what they were doing. You know. And it was great. So I said, “Okay, once a year from now on I will play with you.” And that was a good thing because it showcased the jazz band and it was a good recruiting thing for anybody that was at the Count Basie concert that might want to come to U.K. Because the band was

pretty good. And I played a solo with them. And Count Basie asked to see me. And I said, “Wow, I’d love to meet him.” So he says, “Wow, young man, you sound really good” he says, “you know if we have an opening on the Basie band, would you like to come and play lead trumpet with us?” I said, “Well you know I’d really love to do that but I can’t do it during the year because I really love what I’m doing here. But thanks for asking,” I said, “that’s a great thing” you know what I mean? So I’m happy just to get asked you know is like having done it almost. I know you’ve got to go.
